title: Electromagnetic spectrum; Doppler effect; Superposition, interference and coherence
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: W06-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; W06-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W11-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W06-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: W02-1#N.2, W06-1#N.2b, W02-1#N.9b, W06-1#N.8, W02-1#N.14, W06-1#N.11, W06-1#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Constructive interference
items.clue: Meeting in step, crest on crest, so the amplitudes add; heard as loud.

items.label: Path difference
items.clue: Extra distance from one source compared with the other: 0.60 m for 3.00 m and 3.60 m.

items.label: Doppler effect
items.clue: Shift in observed pitch when a source moves: higher when approaching, lower when receding.

items.label: Destructive interference
items.clue: Meeting out of step so that displacements cancel, as when one route is 1.5λ longer; heard as quiet.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which statement describes the nature of electromagnetic waves?

options.text: Oscillations of the particles of the medium they travel through, so they cannot cross a vacuum
Oscillating electric and magnetic fields that travel faster in a vacuum the higher their frequency
Streams of tiny charged particles given out by the source, which can travel through a vacuum
Oscillating electric and magnetic fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel

questions.stem: Two pulses on a rope overlap at point X. At that instant, pulse 1 on its own would displace the rope at X by 2.0 mm downward, and pulse 2 on its own would displace it by 3.0 mm downward. Taking upward as positive, what is the displacement of the rope at X?
Predict first. Which ranking of the wavelengths of four categories of electromagnetic waves, from longest to shortest, is correct?

Two loudspeakers connected to the same signal generator emit sound in phase at a frequency of 500 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m s⁻¹. At which of these path differences is the sound quiet because of destructive interference?
questions.explanation: λ = 0.68 m, and 1.02 m = 1.5λ, a half-odd number of wavelengths: crest meets trough, destructive.

questions.stem: In a vacuum, the microwaves in a speed camera have a wavelength of 3.0 cm, and the light from a yellow lamp has a wavelength of 600 nm. How do their frequencies compare?

options.text: The microwave frequency is 5 × 10⁴ times the light frequency, since f rises with λ.
They are equal, because both waves travel at the same speed, c, in a vacuum.
The light frequency is 5 × 10⁴ times the microwave frequency, since f = c/λ.
The light frequency is higher, because light travels faster than microwaves.

questions.explanation: Same c for both, so f ∝ 1/λ. Ratio = (3.0 × 10⁻² m)/(600 × 10⁻⁹ m) = 5 × 10⁴: the light's frequency is that many times higher.

questions.stem: A 440.0 Hz tuning fork and a second tuning fork are struck together, and a student counts 12 beats in 4.00 s. Which of the following could be the frequency of the second fork?

Two dippers vibrating in phase act as coherent sources S₁ and S₂ on a ripple tank, producing waves of wavelength 2.0 cm. Point P is 31.0 cm from S₁ and 37.0 cm from S₂. What kind of interference occurs at P?

options.text: Destructive: the paths are 15.5λ and 18.5λ, not whole numbers of λ
Destructive: the path difference, 3λ, is an odd number of λ
Neither: maxima occur only where P is equidistant from S₁ and S₂
Constructive: the path difference is 6.0 cm, which is 3λ
